chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr narrated from Asim ibn Humayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does one enter the Sanctuary (Haram) except while in the state of Ihram?' He said, 'No, except for a sick person or one with diarrhea.'

key_terms.مُحْرِمًا: One in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Who is exempt from the requirement of Ihram when entering the Haram?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while entering the Haram in a state of Ihram is the normative requirement, the principle of *rukhsa* (dispensation) applies to those with genuine impediments. Specifically, the Imam exempts the sick and those suffering from diarrhea, highlighting the jurisprudential balance between the sanctity of the shrine and the removal of hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) for individuals unable to perform the ritual properly.
